preparedHeads.Evidence: MW explicitly gives the verb vi-rāj, present virājati, with senses of ruling and shining. This is not the noun virāj or the verb virajyati.

preparedHeads.Gloss: shine; be ensconced; take a seat (honorific)
preparedHeads.Evidence: McGregor derives the Hindi verb by adaptation from virājati and includes the honorific sitting sense. The lexical hyphen is omitted in display transcription.

proposedAssignments.Notes: Proposed learned virāj- family from Sanskrit virājati. McGregor explicitly supports the Hindi adaptation and honorific sitting sense; application to Mewari birājyɔ is a comparative proposal. Possible Hindi mediation is unresolved, not asserted.

proposals.evidence: McGregor p. 927 gives virājnā, adapted from virājati, with an honorific sitting sense. A Sanskrit virājati donor plus the Hindi comparandum now supports a learned-family proposal; precise borrowing route remains to be reviewed.

The survey item 145 is light in weight (halkā, kam-bojh), so a dawn connection would require a gloss mismatch or an unexplained semantic shift. Retain pending user review.
